articles.title: Birmingham's Joe Lycett wants his art exhibition to inspire others
articles.text:
A life-sized pink woolly mammoth, Ozzy Osbourne, and an old phone are among some of the subjects comedian and artist Joe Lycett hopes will inspire others to get creative.

Everything Must Go at Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery was inspired by "things that are no longer with us", he said, describing his first major solo art exhibition as "a neon graveyard, full of colour".

"I want people to come in and go, 'well I could do that', and then go and do it, please, go and do it better," he said.

"It's so good for you and I really get cross when people go, 'oh I'm not really creative'. If you can put pen to paper, you're creative, you can make things."

Lycett has been working on the collection, which opens on Wednesday, over the past year.

He said it sprang from his love of painting animals, then became an "exercise in looking into grief", also honouring friends who had died.

Its centrepiece is the mixed media sculpture of Martin the mammoth, which has ceramic yellow toenails and a latex tongue.

He decided to make it one night "at 4am, which is when all my ideas come".

It was available to buy for £80, he joked, "but you do need to get it out yourself".

The Nokia 2210, an acrylic on canvas, depicts the comedian's favourite-ever phone, and features a message saying, Snobs?, referring to a legendary city nightspot.

He said he was inspired to paint Ozzy after attending his final show at Villa Park last July. "I was so moved by it," he added.

He said it was important to him the exhibition was in his hometown, not only because it was "really convenient" to get there on a new train line from Kings Heath.

"This place is amazing and so much of it is closed off," he said, referring to the 19th Century museum and art gallery.

"This building is grand because when it was built people believed in the arts and spent money on it, and that's because art has value for humans and we should be doing a lot more of that," he said.

Everything Must Go can be seen from Wednesday until 21 February next year, every day during school holidays and between 10:00 BST and 17:00 BST from Tuesday to Sunday.

Lycett's next focus is a new live TV show, The Lycett Arms, coming later this year to Channel 4, and he is also planning a tour for next year.

articles.title: Children of Blood and Bone: First trailer for novel adaptation
articles.text:
Fans of Children of Blood and Bone got a fresh glimpse of stars including Cynthia Erivo, Damson Idris and Lashana Lynch in the first trailer for the film adaptation of the popular fantasy novel.

The young adult novel follows Zélie Adebola as she tries to bring magic back to the mythical kingdom of Orïsha after a ruthless king wiped it out.

It is the first in a trilogy by Nigerian-American author Tomi Adeyemi, who co-wrote the screenplay with Gina Prince-Bythewood, director of Bafta-nominated historical drama The Woman King.

The adaptation is set to be released in January 2027, but Adeyemi has already distanced herself from the project.

The new trailer opens with award-winning actress Lynch as Jumoke, the mother of Zélie, played by South African actress Thuso Mbedu.

Jumoke can be seen kneeling in front of a younger version of her daughter in the desert, telling her: "You must not be afraid."

Alongside clips of forests, pink lakes and people working in a village, a voiceover by Lynch says: "Orisha was once a land where magic flowed through our people."

She then tells her daughter she was "born with a gift greater than you know" as it shows her creating fire with her hands.

However, she explains, "those who feared our power took it away from us" as it shifts to clips of an army storming the village and taking away Jumoke.

Later, Viola Davis's character Lekan tells an older Zélie that she has been training her for years as she believes she can "bring magic back" to the area.

F1 the Movie star Idris also appears as Prince Inan and Wicked actress Erivo portrays Admiral Kaea.

The film's star-studded cast also features Luther actor Idris Elba, Rush singer Ayra Starr, The Hate U Give Amandla Stenberg and Brit Rising Star winner Bukky Bakray among its cast.

Last month, Adeyemi shared photos to her social media channel suggesting tensions between her and the film's producers.

In a post, she said: "There is a reason I will not post anything about the adaptation of my work. That's all."

She also posted a screenshot of a text message apparently sent to Stenberg, who plays Princess Amari in the upcoming film, in which she wrote: "Do not ever use my name in an interview or video again.

"Do not text me. Do not call me."

The production team and Stenberg have been approached for comment.

articles.title: Richard Hammond fined £999 after being caught speeding twice
articles.text:
Former Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond has been fined £999 after being caught speeding twice in three weeks while driving luxury cars.

The 56-year-old was captured driving his Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo at 68mph in a 50mph limit on the A40 in Pencraig, Herefordshire on 2 December.

He was later clocked driving his Bentley Continental GT at 82mph in a 70mph limit on the M50 Rudhall Overbridge, also in Herefordshire, on 22 December.

Hammond pleaded guilty to two speeding charges through his solicitor. Two further charges that he had ignored the police letters and failed to identify himself as the guilty driver were withdrawn by police.

He was also given seven penalty points for his licence at the hearing last week.

Magistrate Ann Minton ordered him to pay a total of £1,771, comprising two fines of £333 and £666, £240 in costs and victim surcharges totalling £532.

Documents from the case show Hammond was first caught speeding by a police officer with a handheld speed camera at just before 13:00 GMT on 2 December and again at about 11:45 on 22 December.

West Mercia Police sent speeding tickets to a Grade II listed Herefordshire castle bought by Hammond in 2012 and a £1m farm estate near Hereford, but the letters were returned marked as "addressee gone away".

He was eventually tracked down to his £2m home near Abergavenny in Wales where more than 30 vehicles were currently registered, the court heard.

Police also set out in the court papers that Hammond had been accused of another driving offence in August last year.

Hammond, who hosted the BBC's Top Gear show with Jeremy Clarkson and James May between 2002 and 2015, received a three-month driving ban in France in 2013 after he and Clarkson were caught speeding while making an episode of the show.

To the charges of ignoring the police letters and failing to identify himself as the guilty driver, he said in a letter to the court read out by his solicitor: "He replied identifying himself as the driver. He sent the reply by First Class post. He posted the reply himself."

The force ultimately opted to withdraw the extra charges, as Hammond was prosecuted and convicted for the speeding.
